text:
Alex: Quick heads-up — I flipped on the linear RoPE scaling profile against Mixtral-8B on the longctx runner and hit a perplexity bump + throughput jitter. Posting raw numbers and a small profile dump so we can triage.

Megan: ugh okay. which workload? eval set or synthetic?

Alex: eval set (webtext-10k, seq=16k warm). Before change: ppl=12.1, p50 token-latency=48ms. After linear-RoPE: ppl=13.9, p50=56ms, p95=180ms (big tail).

Sam: did you also change head/kv dims or just the RoPE exponent?

Alex: only RoPE scaling map: switched from NTK-style to linear with slope=0.00012 for heads>64. No other model weights touched. Kernel selector picked patched faster-attn kernel for step<=2048 and fallback for long steps.

Jordan: paste the kernel selection log?

Alex: sure — snippet from runtime routing log:

```
[2076543210] model=mixtral-8b variant=linear-rope cfg={rope.scale:linear(0.00012)}
kernel_selector: chosen=attn-opt-v2 (fast path) for seq<=2048
kernel_selector: chosen=attn-fallback for seq>2048
kvcache: enabled per_shard, head_slice=8
batching: continuous-batcher max_batch=64 target_latency_ms=70
perf: throughput=720 tok/s (avg) p50=56 p95=180
```

Nikita: two immediate hypotheses: 1) linear RoPE changed magnitude distribution so exact kernel (attn-opt-v2) numerics degrade -> quality drop; 2) head_slice=8 shards the KV in a way that increases synchronization cost for longctx, exacerbating p95.

Megan: agree on (2). we saw similar tail when we increased head slicing for Qwen-7B; KV gather cost scales nonlinearly with slices.

Sam: can you repro with head_slice=1 or 2? also try forcing attn-opt-v2 for long steps to see if kernel switch is the issue.

Alex: repro runs in progress. quick diff I applied to the runner config:

```
# override
runtime.attn_kernel.override_for_seq_ge=8192 -> attn-opt-v2
kv.head_slice=2
batcher.target_latency_ms=60
```

ci-bot: started perf job 2076543210-rls (mixtral-8b, longctx, 3 trials)

Alex: first trial with head_slice=2 + kernel-forced -> ppl=12.25, p50=50ms, p95=92ms. That's promising — ppl back near baseline and tail reduced.

Jordan: that's a strong signal that head sharding was the main perf/regression vector. quality recovering suggests kernel numerics also matter but secondary.

Nikita: let's also dump kv memory access profile (per-head stalls) — I suspect increased L2->L3 traffic when slices>4 leading to contention.

Megan: want a diff of activation magnitudes (attn weights) too. if scaling map changed rot-phase magnitudes, some kernels with fused attention may quantize differently and cause small softmax shifts -> ppl moves.

Alex: attached small activations excerpt:```
attn_weight_mean by head (baseline vs linear-rope):
head0: 0.0021 -> 0.0019
head1: 0.0019 -> 0.0016
head2: 0.0023 -> 0.0018
... (mean drop ~10-15%)
```

Sam: that magnitude drop aligns with fewer saturation events in softmax, but a consistent bias could still shift ppl. we should run a tiny eval comparing token-level KL across outputs.

Jordan: ops-wise, quick fixes: revert head_slice to 2 for longctx Mixtral variants, add an automatic guard in kernel selector that prefers single-shard KV below a certain step size distribution, and add an alert when ppl delta > 0.5 after rollout.

Alex: I'll open a small change request. Proposed rollout plan: canary 5% with head_slice=2 + linear-rope, monitor ppl and p95; if pass after 6h, ramp. If ppl regresses >0.4 -> rollback to NTK mapping.

Megan: add a perf regression alert wired into Redwood-Optimize so engineers get actionable suggestion (head_slice=2).

Nikita: also capturing recommended safe ranges per-model in the model catalog: for Mixtral-8B linear-rope slope <=0.00015 and head_slice<=2 for longctx. For Mistral-7B keep NTK default unless head_dim>128.

Sam: can we add a microbenchmark that runs kernel numerics comparison (attn-opt-v2 vs fallback) on a set of sequence lengths (512, 2048, 8192, 16384) and reports max per-token KL and latency? put it in eng-runtime perf harness.

Alex: will add. quick action items: 1) revert prod route to head_slice=2 for Mixtral longctx (Alex) 2) add kernel-selector guard + perf microbenchmark (Sam) 3) add per-model safe-range doc entry (Nikita) 4) upgrade Redwood-Optimize to surface head-slice suggestion (Megan).

Jordan: sounds good. small note — double-check quantization path; some quant kernels assume NTK normalization so mixing mapping approaches may interact badly with 8-bit matmuls.

Alex: noted. I'll include a quick quant check in the canary.

ci-bot: perf job 2076543210-rls completed: 3/3 trials healthy for head_slice=2 config; artifacts at https://ci.redwood-inference/perf/2076543210

Megan: nice. anyone want to pair on the microbenchmark tomorrow?

Sam: I'll join. 10am PT?

Alex: thanks all — will open the PR and post link here when ready. :thumbsup:
